```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab02", title = "Time Series Graphics")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Which plot shows the same quarter across years side by side?",
  q2 = "Beer lag-4 points in a lag plot tend to look:",
  q3 = "Which Beer quarter looks highest? Cite the seasonal or subseries plot."
)
```

## What you will do

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `learnr`, `fpp3`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## Time and seasonal plots
```{r graphics-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
library(fpp3)
aus_production |> autoplot(Beer)
aus_production |> gg_season(Beer, labels = "both")
aus_production |> gg_subseries(Beer)
aus_production |> gg_lag(Beer, geom = "point")
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("gg_season() / gg_subseries()", correct = TRUE),
  answer("autoplot() only"),
  answer("ACF plot"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Positively associated (seasonal memory)", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Scattered like white noise"),
  answer("Exactly on a flat horizontal line"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Tourism stretch (optional)
```{r tourism-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=10}
# Sum regions so autoplot is one clear series (not 20+ lines + a huge legend)
vic_holiday <- tourism |>
  filter(Purpose == "Holiday", State == "Victoria") |>
  index_by(Quarter) |>
  summarise(Trips = sum(Trips), .groups = "drop")

vic_holiday |>
  autoplot(Trips) +
  labs(title = "Victoria holiday trips (all regions summed)", y = "Trips")
```

```{r q3}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "e.g. Q4 looks highest because …",
  trim = TRUE
)
```
